memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses and Aaron brought together all the elders of the Israelites, and Aaron told them everything the Lord had said to Moses. He also performed the signs before the people, and they believed. And when they heard that the Lord was concerned about them and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshipped." - Exodus 4:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Remember where this chapter began. Moses' very first objection was, what if they do not believe me? Now the chapter closes with the words: and they believed.

His great fear simply did not happen. Most of them never do.

But look closely at what actually moved these people. It was not primarily the signs. The text says that when they heard the Lord was concerned about them and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshipped.

What broke them was not power. It was compassion. The news that God had noticed — after four hundred years of silence, God had seen — brought a nation to its knees.

That is still what melts hard hearts. Not arguments, not spectacle, but the news that God sees us and cares. And the fullest proof of that came when Christ was moved with compassion for crowds who were like sheep without a shepherd (Mt 9:36), and then gave His life for them.

God has seen your misery too. Let that bring you to worship today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has the news that God sees and cares moved me to worship recently?
2. What fear of mine, like Moses', never actually came true?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You have seen me and You care. I bow before You today with a grateful heart. Amen.
